youtube.title: Why Honeycomb Cells Are Always Hexagons 🐝 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Honeybees build their honeycomb out of hexagonal cells. A hexagon tiles a flat surface with no gaps and uses less wall than any other shape that holds the same area, which saves wax. Wax is costly for bees to make, taking roughly six pounds of honey for one pound of wax. Mathematicians suspected hexagons were the best for over 1,600 years, and Thomas Hales proved it in 1999.
